dedupe_keys.name: code to process harmonized gap filled datasets from 20 urban flux tower sites for the urban plumber projects

description: The Urban-PLUMBER collaboration at UNSW Sydney publishes the processing code for its 20-site urban flux dataset. Python scripts harmonise observations, apply quality checks, correct reanalysis bias and fill gaps to create forcing series at 30- or 60-minute resolution. Site wrappers retain local morphology and surface-cover metadata, while output series are written as NetCDF and text. The documented application spans urban sites in multiple countries with different observation periods, and corrected ERA5 inputs cover 1990–2020. GitHub exposes the code under Apache-2.0, free to reuse; the archived release has a generic other-open label. Raw site observations and other large inputs are held separately. A limitation is that reproduction therefore requires input access, suitable dependencies and inspection of each site’s corrections. The workflow can prepare urban energy-balance simulation forcing. It complements the published harmonised data by exposing its processing decisions. No code was executed.
